newsitem.title: USA: Barnett takeover talk seen heating up.
newsitem.headline: Barnett takeover talk seen heating up.

text.p: Takeover talk centering on Jacksonville, Fla.-based Barnett Banks Inc will probably heat up after news Wednesday that chairman and chief executive Charles Rice has taken a medical leave to enter an alcohol treatment facility, analysts said.
"This will set off a wave of takeover rumors because Charlie has been a key force in keeping the bank independent," said Richard Bove, analyst at Raymond James & Associates.

Barnett, a $40 billion asset bank and a powerhouse in Florida, said in a news release that Rice would take a "short term" leave after informing the board of directors he voluntarily admitted himself to a facility.
Bove, who said he last saw Rice at an analysts meeting in Boca Raton, Fla. in November, said the news came as a surprise.
He said Rice was always "totally in control," answering questions quickly and to the point. "I never would have guessed he had a substance abuse problem," Bove said.
Bove said although the takeover talk was an inevitable "outside the bank" issue, from the "inside the bank" perspective Barnett is in excellent hands in the interim.
Barnett said in its news release that Allen Lastinger Jr., president and chief operating officer, would assume Rice's role on a temporary basis.

"Lastinger changed the whole focus of the bank away from making acquisitions to a product emphasis," Bove said. The analyst said working with chief financial officer Charles Newman, top talent was recruited from all over the U.S., elaborate technology was installed and the bank got out of slow-growth businesses.
Bove said he was maintaining the buy rating on Barnett that he has had for a period of years.
A Barnett spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
The news that Rice was taking a temporary leave as announced moments after the New York Stock Exchange close.
Barnett shares closed up 3/8 at 50-3/4 on the NYSE and finished at 51 on the Pacific Stock Exchange, which has a later closing time.
